claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son, Alex.

To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about your circumstances.

**First, could you tell me: What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old - he was born in 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So Alex was born in 2016 and is currently 8 years old.

**Next, I'd like to know: Are you the parent or guardian with primary responsibility for Alex, or is there another arrangement in place?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and he lives at home with me. I have primary responsibility for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. I can see you have primary responsibility for Alex and he lives with you.

**Now, could you tell me: Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?** (This relates to residency and immigration status requirements for Child Benefit.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, yes. I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that. You're a British citizen and living in the UK.

**Next question: Is Alex a British citizen, or does he have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Both you and Alex are British citizens.

**One more question: Are you currently working or studying, or are you receiving any benefits or allowances?** (This helps me understand your overall circumstances, as there are certain income-related considerations for Child Benefit.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working, yes. Why do you need to know that for Child Benefit eligibility?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! I ask because while Child Benefit itself isn't means-tested (meaning your income doesn't affect whether you can claim it), there is a High Income Child Benefit Charge that applies if your income exceeds a certain threshold. This means you might still be eligible to receive Child Benefit, but you could owe tax on it if your income is high enough. It's important information for your overall eligibility picture.

**So, to clarify: What is your approximate annual income?** (This will help me determine if the High Income Child Benefit Charge would apply to you.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see, that makes sense. My income is around £45,000 a year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. With an income of around £45,000 a year, the High Income Child Benefit Charge wouldn't apply to you, as that charge only kicks in at higher income thresholds.

**Just to confirm one final detail: Is Alex in full-time education or training?** (This is important as Child Benefit eligibility continues while children are in approved education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8, so yes, he's in primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to make a determination.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (born in 2016)
- He lives with you and you have primary responsibility for him
- Both you and Alex are British citizens
- Your income is approximately £45,000 per year
- Alex is in full-time education (primary school)

Let me provide you with my eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

You meet all the requirements:
- Alex is under 16 and in full-time education
- You both have British citizenship
- Alex lives with you and you have primary responsibility for him
- Your income is below the threshold where the High Income Child Benefit Charge would apply

You should be able to proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already, you can make a claim through the appropriate government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?
